title: Improved long gaps between consecutive primes
abstract: Formalizes the unconditional lower bound showing that, for all sufficiently large X, the largest gap between consecutive primes below X is at least a positive constant times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2. The development includes the short-translates sieve proposition, divisor coefficient estimates, truncated product weights, moment bounds, and the Erdos--Rankin covering argument used to derive the headline result.

informal.LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_prime_gaps: There are a positive constant c and a real threshold X0 such that for every X at least X0, some pair of consecutive indexed primes below X has gap greater than c times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2.
informal.LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_gap_theorem: For all sufficiently large X, there are consecutive primes p < q with q at most X and q - p at least a fixed positive multiple of the improved long-gap scale.
informal.LongGapsBetweenPrimes.short_translates: For all sufficiently large x, every sufficiently sparse subset S of an interval of length between x and x(log x)^2 has a translate b + Q(x)t + S consisting entirely of composite numbers, with 1 <= t <= exp x.
